title: Colored knot Floer homology: structures and examples: the module structure over the cable algebra (Theorem 5.1)
author: Akram Alishahi, Eugene Gorsky, Beibei Liu
work: Colored knot Floer homology: structures and examples
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the theorem that the space Tw_D(L) is a triply graded module over the cable algebra CA_n, printed as Theorem 5.1 of "Colored knot Floer homology: structures and examples" (source0.tex lines 2448--2451, source label thm: cabled module), delivered together with the article's own complete proof at source0.tex lines 2453--2523 (71 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The theorem is one of the article's main structural results: it is announced in the introduction (line 485) as the step that upgrades the unlink computation to an arbitrary link, and it is the result from which the article's coloured module structure and its localization theorem are derived. The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span. It defines the action of the generators a_k on Tw_D(L) by the cobordism maps phi_k, and it verifies the two families of relations by comparing the general link with the unknot. On the geometric side it introduces the link L'_m with an extra pair of basepoints per component, extends the colouring, identifies cHFL(L'_m) with the quotient of cHFL(L_m) tensor a polynomial ring by the ideal of the differences U_i - U'_i, and shows that the quasi-stabilization cobordism composed with that identification is the identity; it then exhibits the cobordisms C_m, C'_m, B_m, C_{b,m} and C_{O_n,m} and proves, by isotoping the attaching circle of a 2-handle past band attachments (following the cited Proposition 3.13 of the article's own reference AGL) and then applying the naturality of link Floer homology (the cited Zemke), that phi_k^L factors as a band-attachment map composed with the identity tensor phi_k^O composed with a birth map. The linear relations for phi_k^L follow from those for phi_k^O by R_{UV}-linearity, and the quadratic relations and the commutativity of the maps follow by repeating the isotopy for the composition of two full twists; the two cited inputs (AGL Proposition 3.13 and the naturality theorem of Zemke) are standard published results named at the point of use, exactly as the article names them. Every step of the argument is carried out in the retained span, and the only internal dependency is the article's Theorem 4.6, whose statement is retained here as context. The argument is a research-level verification in link Floer homology: it needs decorated link cobordisms, the functoriality and naturality of the full link Floer package, the basepoint-moving and quasi-stabilization isomorphisms and a genuine handle-slide argument, and it is the technical heart of the article's structure theorem rather than a routine computation. It is rated H2 rather than H3 because it is a verification by reduction to the established unlink case, with the heavy geometric input delegated to published results that the article cites, rather than the introduction of a new method.
